recipes.name: Braseltouille - Meatatarian Ratatouille
ingredients_raw: 3 yellow squash, halved lengthwise and sliced
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Cook and stir sausage in a large skillet over medium heat until sausage is crumbly and no longer pink, about 10 minutes. Transfer sausage to a large bowl using a slotted spoon; set aside. Reserve 1 tablespoon drippings in skillet; drain excess grease. Cook and stir bell pepper, onion, and garlic in drippings until bell pepper is soft, about 8 minutes; transfer to the bowl with sausage.

Add olive oil to the hot skillet; cook and stir yellow squash and zucchini until slightly softened, about 8 minutes. Stir in tomatoes and Italian seasoning; season with salt and black pepper. Bring to a boil; simmer until squash are tender, 10 to 15 minutes.

Stir sausage and vegetables into skillet; increase heat to high and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium; cook, stirring often, until liquid has reduced, about 15 minutes. Transfer sausage mixture to a 9x13-inch baking dish; sprinkle with Cheddar cheese.
Bake in the preheated oven until mixture is bubbly and cheese has melted and begun to brown, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Braseltouille - Meatatarian Ratatouille
raw_recipe.description: Braseltouille—meatatarian ratatouille recipe includes ratatouille flavors from tomatoes, zucchini, and yellow squash, with sausage and Cheddar cheese.

review.reviewBody: Scrumptious ! Sausage, cheese, spicy, what's not to like. I've been looking for a recipe like this and it was everything I wished for. When you make this be sure to take the cook's advice and strain the juice, you'll be glad you did.

We were looking for a filling veggie dish that was on the healthier side. I found this and was happy to see that it did not include eggplant as a traditional ratatouille does. We aren't eggplant fans but I expect that if you do like eggplant, you could easily add some to this and it would be fine. I adjusted ingredients a little based on what I had on hand. I used kielbasa rather than ground sausage. I sliced each piece in half lengthwise, then sliced the halves into thin "half moons". Because kielbasa cooks off alot less fat than ground sausage, I added a little more olive oil than is called for. I omitted the green pepper because we don't care for cooked green peppers. (Ironic that the only two vegetables that we don't care for would both be in this dish!) I used a whole onion because we love onions and to make up for the missing green pepper. I used 3 zuchinni rather than 2 along with the 3 yellow squash. I used my large cast iron skillet and it was FULL. I used bottled minced garlic (and probably more than 2 cloves worth!) Once I added the one 14.5 ounce can of tomatoes, I could tell that it needed more, so I used a second can. I simmered the veggies partially covered for 20 minutes or so, then decided that rather than heating up the oven, I'd do like another reviewer suggested and just cook it on top of the stove. After simmering and stirring for a good little while and adjusting the seasonings, it was missing something, so I went to my fave "red sauce

Yum. I have tomato, zucchini, and squash growing this year , and was looking for a way to use them up. I did make a few changes. I used one large zucchini, 2 squash, 3 big tomatoes ,and a few cherry tomatoes. No canned. I did have half a jar of Ragu spaghetti sauce I threw in. And of course 1 lb of mild Italian sausage. At the end of the stovetop cooking, I added about 1 cup of shredded parmesan, and then once it was in the casserole dish, I topped it with shredded mozarella instead of cheddar. It was all about using up what I already had and this recipe worked great!

It was my first time making ratatouille - didn't know what it was until a client gave me a bag of fresh fall vegetables and recommended it. I made it with Italian Turkey Sausage and added egg plant. Couldn't stop picking at the pan after dinner. I simplified the recipe. Instead cooking this and setting it aside and cooking that and setting it aside - I cooked it all in one pot. Knowing how much time it takes to cook each veg. helped.

Since I made some changes to this I'm giving it 5 stars on principle-- I added some eggplant to the mix and used mozzarella as well as a tiny bit of grated aged provolone since I didn't have enough cheddar on hand. I'll make sure to have cheddar on hand the next time I make this. I didn't cook the squash on the stovetop nearly as long as the instructions called for fear of overcooking, and the texture turned out perfect according to my tastes. I also added a little beef stock to it before going into the oven because I thought it would have been a little dry otherwise. It was very tasty and I will definitely make this again! Thanks for sharing!

Very good and different. I added eggplant and cooked zucchini, squash and eggplant in chicken broth...I used breakfast sausage and stirred a handful each of sharp cheddar, mild cheddar, and Mexican cheese in addition to placing it on top. Very flavorful!

This was delicious!! I made it with smoked sausage because that’s what i had. And instead of a can of tomatoes i used tomatoes picked from my garden, along with the squash & zucchini. I made the recipe just as it was written, except once i combined the meat with the squash—I skipped that second simmer and went straight to the oven step. This was fantastic and smelled wonderful too!

Delicious! I didn't have any canned tomatoes, so I just diced three or four roma tomatoes and simmered them for a little bit before tossing them in. 

I don't much care for steamed squash, so I was thrilled that this turned out to be so tasty and easy to make. Since I used my food processor to slice the squash, and zucchini very thin (2 mm slices), I also shortened the stove top cooking times a little bit. It still turned out perfectly.

A very flexible recipe.

I used nenni's Italian pork sausage recipe, tomato products left from canning and didn't use the oven. I cooked as directed except stirred in the cheese and served instead of topping and placing in the oven. I like to keep some bite to my summer squash and thought the bake time would push it too far for our preference. This was great on toasted hoagie slices.

Absolutely fabulous! My neighbor had given me some zucchini and yellow squash from the farmers' market, and I am so glad I found this recipe. I used kielbasa, because that's what I had. I chopped purple, red, yellow and green peppers and a whole onion and used a can of fire roasted tomatoes. Italian seasoning, pepper and a bit of salt were perfect. I did the whole thing on the stove, rather than heating up the whole house by turning on the oven. I mixed the cheese in at the last, and served it to a very grateful hubby. He gave it the 5 stars, before I had even taken a bite.

Great recipe to make on Sunday and eat throughout the week. I didn't have Italian seasoning on hand so I used 1tbsp of basil, parsley, and oregano. I also used ground turkey instead of pork, added 1tsp cayenne to add some heat, and used Parmesan cheese instead of cheddar. A very easy and delicious recipe!
Delicious 😋
This was delicious! Next time I'll add eggplant. Couldn't stop eating it. Thanks!
Made it w/o meat and added eggplant and used red bell pepper severed with pasta.

I changed nothing. My mom loves ratatouille, so I made this for her/us for Mother's Day. Mine wanted to be drier than some others who said to drain, I actually had to add a little water. She loved it, my dad (not a ratatouille fan) loved it, I loved it.

I simmered and reduced the liquid in the saucepan for a long time till it was almost gummy, rather than pour it off. I added a bit of red pepper flakes and celery seed, too. Yummy yummy! My family loved this!
Don't like tomatoes, I did like the squash and zucchini part. Very good meal.
Super yummy veggie recipe!

I made a few changes to the recipe because of my husband's dietary restrictions. We used basmati rice, Italian seasoning instead of salt and whole wheat Panko breading instead of bread crumbs. Our sauce was also low sodium, home-made with tomato sauce, tomato paste, diced tomatoes and some Italian seasoning. The husband and kids really liked it and requested that it be put on the regular rotation.

5 stars for ease and taste. Able to adjust vegetables as you see fit. I added cubed eggplant and mushrooms, then needed a 10 x 14 pan. A lot of chopping prep work but at least it will last us two meals. Also broiled the vegetables instead of stovetop. Served with baked potatoes, a perfect side.
